WHAT EACH STAMP DOES TO THE NODE READING IT (G-39, raised by arch-review and panel-codex-arch). The brief rendered `- CONTRACT-PARTIAL` and stopped there. Only TESTS-THIN and FMT-DIRTY carried a sentence saying what followed from them, and they carried it as separate template blocks — so a lens was handed a list of words it had to interpret, and I-49 requires a stamp to state its effect where it is stated at all. A stamp whose consequence a node has to guess is a fact about the run that changes no behaviour, which is the definition of an inert guarantee.

One entry per stamp any script emits; check-stamp-consequences (tests) fails if the two sets diverge, because a stamp added without a sentence here is exactly the defect this file closes. Written in the second person, because the reader is the node.

UNTESTED: `commands.test` is empty: no suite ran. Test coverage is not available to you as mitigation, and 'the tests would catch this' is not a finding you can close on.
UNBENCHED: `commands.bench` is empty: nothing was measured. Every performance finding in this run is static-risk-only and is recorded at LOW — except a §6 invariant, which is never capped. Do not report a slowdown as measured.
TESTS-THIN: The declared suite reported fewer than five tests. You may NOT cite test coverage as mitigation for anything in this run — a suite that thin does not carry that weight, and the run already records the fact.
FMT-DIRTY: `commands.fmt_check` already failed, and that fact is recorded. Formatting findings are INADMISSIBLE in this run — reporting them re-reports a known result as a discovery, and buries the findings nobody has seen yet.
TESTS-FAILING: The declared suite RAN AND FAILED, and the gate is already FAIL because of it. Reporting the failing suite as a finding re-reports a known result as a discovery. What is worth reporting is anything the failures conceal: a behaviour no test covers is not made safer by the tests being red.
TESTS-UNCOUNTED: The suite ran, but its output matched no format this framework can count, so the number of tests is UNKNOWN — not zero, and not thin. Neither 'well covered' nor 'barely covered' is available to you as a premise; cite what a specific test asserts, or say the coverage is unknown.
UNSWEPT-DIFF: This run's scope was ASSERTED BY A PERSON (--full-sweep), not derived from a diff. So the paths you were given are the ones someone chose to review, and they are not guaranteed to be the ones that changed — a file changed since the base commit may sit outside them, unread by any lens. What it changes for you: your verdict covers the declared surface, not the change. Do not write that something is unaffected by a change you were never shown.
UNREQUESTED: No approved request governs this work and none could be inferred. You are judging code against no stated criteria, so contract-audit does not run (it is SKIPPED, its condition being a request) and you may not report a gap against a requirement nobody wrote.
REQUEST-DISCOVERED: `doc_roles.request` was empty and new-run FOUND an approved request in .claude/requests/ and used it. The criteria you are judging against were discovered, not declared — so a mismatch between the code and that document may mean the run picked the wrong document, and that possibility belongs in your finding rather than outside it.
REQUEST-MISSING: A request document was declared and is not readable at the declared path. The criteria this run claims to judge against do not exist; any finding of yours that cites them is citing nothing.
REQUEST-INFERRED: No approved request existed, so request-capture INFERRED one from the diff and the history. You are judging conformance against a reconstruction of what someone probably wanted, not against what anyone said — contract-audit is capped for exactly this reason (a §6 invariant finding is never capped). A mismatch may be a wrong inference rather than a defect, and your finding must say which you mean.
INTENT-PINNED: The criteria in intent.md were REUSED from an earlier run whose inputs hashed identically, not derived for this one. They are as binding as freshly derived criteria — the inputs are provably unchanged — and the run records which run derived them, which is the thread to pull if a criterion looks wrong for the work in front of you.
INTENT-DRIFT: intent.md changed after this run froze it. The criteria you are judging against are not the criteria that were pinned, so the run is BLOCKED at the gate regardless of what any node reports. Report what you found; do not treat a clean result as a verdict, because this run cannot produce one.
CONTRACT-PARTIAL: Tracked files exist that no contract glob declares — source, tests or docs the contract says nothing about. The declared surface is not the tree: a file absent from your scope may be absent because nobody declared it, not because nobody writes it, so do not conclude from silence that a path is unused.
COVERAGE-UNKNOWN: Whether every tracked file is declared by a contract glob was not checked: listing the tracked files failed, and run.json's contract_coverage_unknown says why. Undeclared files may or may not exist, so treat the declared surface as possibly not the tree, as under CONTRACT-PARTIAL, and do not conclude from silence that a path is unused.
UNCAPPED-BUDGET: One or more spend ceilings are empty, so no dollar limit is enforced on this run. Nothing about your review changes — the stamp exists so a reader knows the run was not bounded, and each uncapped tier is named in the gate's not_checked[].
PANEL-ABSENT: The cross-family panel is off, so no independent-family reviewer is shadowing you. Same-family agreement is one opinion counted twice; your verdict stands alone and nothing downstream will contradict it. Weigh that when you report OK.
PANEL-NO-SAFE-SURFACE: No external reviewer ran in this run: the directory the arms read could not be built safely — its working state was over review.panel_snapshot_max_mb, its framework was incomplete, or the snapshot could not be taken or shown free of links — and the run's panel lines say which. The repository itself is never handed over instead. Every arm is recorded SKIPPED and no dispute was adjudicated. What it changes for you: nothing from another model family will corroborate or contradict your findings here — your verdict stands alone, as when the panel is off.
SKILLS-SHADOWED: A skill name in this project collides with one the engine spawns, so a node may have been handed the project's skill instead of the framework's. Any node behaving unlike its brief describes is explained by this before it is explained by a defect.
TREE-MOVED: The tree changed after this run was minted. Line numbers in your findings may no longer point at the code you read, and a file you cite may have been rewritten since the freeze — cite the excerpt, not just the coordinates.
CONSUMER-LENS: a lens declared by the PROJECT (graph_contract.lenses), instructed by a file in the tree under review rather than by this framework. Its findings are coverage, not authority: basis is convention only, its verdict cannot exceed RISK, it is never required, and it cannot raise a §6 invariant — the same treatment an external arm gets, and for the same reason. If you are that lens, hold to your own instructions AND to this brief; where they disagree, this brief wins and the disagreement is worth reporting.
TESTS-DID-NOT-RUN: The declared test command exited non-zero WITHOUT running any tests — a collection or import error, a missing dependency, a runner that never started. Nothing was tested, which is different from tests being red: there are no failures to reason about and no coverage to rely on. Treat the suite as absent. Do not report the suite itself as a finding, and do not treat any behaviour as covered because tests exist on disk — they did not execute.
TESTS-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN: The declared test command exited non-zero and its output could not be parsed, or the command was stopped before it finished, so whether any test ran is UNKNOWN — the runner may have printed in a format this engine does not recognise. This is neither a red suite nor an absent one: do not reason about failures (none were read) and do not treat any behaviour as covered (nothing confirmed it executed). The run is capped and the gap is named; report only what you verified yourself.
TESTS-TIMED-OUT: The declared test command was KILLED by this engine at its own deadline — it started and did not finish. That is not a red suite and not a missing one: no failure was read, and nothing was confirmed to have passed. Do not treat any behaviour as covered, and do not report the suite itself as a finding. The operator needs to size the timeout, which is a different instruction from fixing a broken install.
CONTRACT-STALE: This project's graph_contract declares OLDER semantics than the engine running this review implements. Its keys are spelled correctly, so nothing else can detect this: a value may now mean something the operator never agreed to. Do not treat a contract-derived guarantee as confirmed, and where a finding depends on what a key means, say which meaning you assumed.

Do not treat a passing suite as established fact here; where a finding turns on the tests having passed, say that the evidence was reused under an inferred freshness claim.

This is not the same as a command being absent from the contract -- these commands exist and were not executed, and the gate names each one.

Nothing about YOUR review changes: you are worth exactly what you are worth in a full review, you hold the same evidence discipline, and your verdict is not capped for this. What changes is what the RUN may be taken to establish -- the dimensions nobody ran found nothing because nobody looked. So do not write that something is sound overall, or that a concern outside your lens was considered; report what your lens found and let the gate carry the scope.

COMMIT-CHECK: Something the runner did not commit as reported, each named in the run's commit_check by its kind: the node did not finish OK (node-failed); its report was missing or named another run (report-mismatch), or the reviewed run's confirmed groups could not be read (confirmed-unknown); a group not confirmed in the reviewed run (unconfirmed-group, where a symptom of a confirmed root is judged as its root and refused when that root is not reported), deferred by the operator (deferred-group), reported not fixed (not-committable), whose red-before-green is not on disk (evidence-refused), or sharing a file or cluster with any of those, or a symptom whose root is one of those (shared-with-refused); the deferred findings' locations could not be read (deferred-file-unchecked); a path the node changed that no planned cluster carries (left-in-tree); a cluster with a refused file (refused-file), or with no source file, a reported test it did not find, or a group with no red and no declaration (refused-cluster); a commit made during the node's run (stray-commit); the candidate's declared checks refused it (full-run-red), or the tree held more than the candidate (tree-not-candidate); a commit git or a hook rejected (hook-rejected), and one whose unstaging failed too (reset-failed); a commit that landed with its sha unread (commit-unrecorded), or with a file a hook rewrote after the check (committed-differs); a cluster committed with no test (committed-without-test). A cluster committed with no test because every group in it declared no possible red (no_red) is named too. {{rule_no_red}} The declared-no-red record does not stamp COMMIT-CHECK, nor does readmitted (groups the evidence gate refused on the first run, planned by --retry-commits --readmit-evidence once it admits them); it and committed-without-test are withdrawn when the commit does not land. A refused cluster set aside for the full check whose bytes could not be written back stops the run with its copies kept (set-aside-unrestored). Three more kinds are notes, not failures, and do not stamp: set-aside-kept (a refused cluster that could not be set aside, so its edits stay and may block the others), deferred-file (a planned group's file also holds a finding the operator deferred) and merged (two clusters that share a file, committed as one). Uncommitted changes stay in the working tree, unstaged — except where the reset failed, which leaves the cluster's files staged and says so. A review of the diff should treat those fixes as unverified.
